note: A contract may be CLOSED only when every proof below exists in the tree. scripts/contract-gate.sh enforces that: a claim with no test behind it is a claim, not a control.

contracts.invariant: Identical inputs produce byte-identical output, and the stored derivation re-derives from the file itself
contracts.measure: two consecutive builds over the fixture feed, byte comparison, then `dozor verify`

contracts.invariant: A released NORA loads the output and enforces it, with no NORA change
contracts.measure: run the published NORA image against a generated blocklist, assert 403 and that the reason string survives

contracts.invariant: An unreadable feed or an empty inventory never overwrites an existing blocklist
contracts.measure: missing feed -> exit 2, empty inventory -> exit 3, previous file byte-identical afterwards

contracts.invariant: A version the matcher cannot decide is reported, never treated as safe
contracts.measure: an unparsable version in the inventory appears in x-dozor-unmatched and in no rule

contracts.invariant: An expired exception fails the build instead of renewing itself
contracts.measure: policy with expires in the past -> exit 4

contracts.invariant: A wholly-malicious package collapses to one `version: "*"` rule, and a partly-malicious one does not
contracts.measure: fixture with both shapes; assert the rule set

contracts.invariant: Advisories from another ecosystem never leak into the blocklist
contracts.measure: a PyPI advisory in the npm fixture produces no rule

contracts.invariant: Peak RSS on the full npm feed stays under 100 MB
contracts.evidence: 2026-09-05: 173 MB peak, 24.9 MB retained index. The gap is transient build allocation, not data. Reserving capacity up front and streaming the output writer are the open items.

contracts.invariant: Scan-on-publish (a synchronous verdict on push) is out of scope
contracts.measure: n/a — would require a resident service with an in-memory index, which D-ADR-1 forbids
